Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 106, verse 1–4:

Meccan, and it has seventy-three letters, seventeen words, and four verses.

Nafil ibn Raqim ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Babi informed me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Balkhi related to us, saying: Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Karmi related to us, saying: Asbat ibn al-Yasa' related to us, saying:

Yahya ibn Ubaydullah al-Sulami related to us, saying: Nuh ibn Abi Maryam related to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah of Li-ilaafi Quraysh will be given the reward of ten good deeds, equal to the number of those who circumambulated the Ka'bah and performed i'tikaf in it" [260] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/449.]].

And al-Husayn informed me, saying: Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halwani related to us, saying: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Thabit, who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Atiq informed me, from Sa'id ibn Umar ibn Ju'dah, from his father, from his grandmother Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah favoured Quraysh with seven qualities that He gave to no one before them and will give to no one after them: Allah favoured Quraysh in that I am of them, prophethood is among them, the hijabah (custodianship of the Ka'bah) is among them, the siqayah (provision of water to pilgrims) is among them, He gave them victory over the elephant, they worshipped Allah, glorified be He, for twenty years with none worshipping Him besides them, and Allah revealed a surah concerning them in which no one other than them is mentioned" [261] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 12/27.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

For the covenant (li-ilaafi) of Quraysh, their covenant.

The reciters differed regarding it. Abdullah ibn Amir read (li-alaaf), with hamza, shortened vowel, and without a yā' (ي). Abu Ja'far read (ilaaf) without hamza, seeking only lightness (li-ilaafi), with the yā' hamzated and elongated. As for their reading (ilaaf): al-Umari related from Abu Ja'far, and al-Balkhi from Ibn Kathir, (ilfihim) with the lām sukun and without a yā'. Confirming this reading is what

al-Husayn ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Khunays related to us, saying: Abu Khadijah Ahmad ibn Dawud related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan ibn Layth, from Shamir ibn Hawshab, from Asma', who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) [recite]: "Ilfihim rihlat al-shita' wa al-sayf" [262] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/394.]].

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan related with his chain from Abu Ja'far, and al-Walid from the people of Syria (ilafihim), with hamza, shortened vowel, and without a yā'. Muhammad ibn Habib al-Hamawi related from Abu Yusuf al-A'sha, from Abu Bakr, from Asim (i'alfihim), with two hamzas, the first kasrah and the second sukun. The rest read (iilaafihim).

Sa'id ibn al-Ma'afa informed us, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Abu Karnab related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Abu Makki, from Ikrimah, that he used to read (iliyalaf Quraysh alfihim).

Some of them counted the two surahs as one; among them Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and there is no separation between them in his mushaf.

Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: We had an imam who did not separate them, and he would recite them together. Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi said: I prayed the Maghrib behind Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and he recited in the first rak'ah "Wa al-tini wa al-zaytun," and in the second "Alam tara" and "Li-ilaafi Quraysh."

They differed regarding the cause that brings in this lām. Al-Farra' said: it is connected to the preceding surah, for He, exalted is He, reminded the people of Makkah of His great blessing upon them in what He did to the Abyssinians; then He said: "li-ilaafi Quraysh," meaning: We did that to the companions of the elephant as a blessing from Us upon Quraysh, that is, Our blessing upon them in their journeys of winter and summer. It is as if He said: a blessing upon a blessing, so the lām carries the meaning of (ila, "to").

Al-Razi and al-Akhfash said: it is the lām of wonder. The meaning is: "Wonder at the covenant of Quraysh, the journey of winter and summer, and their abandonment of worship of the Lord of this House," and then He commanded them to worship Him.

This is like one saying in speech: "For Zayd, and our honouring him," in the manner of wonder, meaning: I marvel at that. When the Arabs bring this lām, they suffice with it as evidence of wonder, making the verb apparent in it, like the words of the poet:

"Does it deceive you that they said Qurrah is a poet? O father of him, of a ʿarīf and a poet!"

That is, wonder at Qurrah being a poet.

It was also said that it is the lām of purpose (kay), its meaning being "fa-ja'alahum ka-'asfin ma'kul" (He made them like eaten chaff) "to bring Quraysh together," so the destruction of the companions of the elephant was the cause of the continuance of Quraysh's covenant and the order of their condition and the wealth of their people. Al-Zajjaj said: it refers to what follows it, its estimate being: "liya'budu rabba hadha al-bayt li-ilaafi rihlat al-shita' wa al-sayf" (so that they may worship the Lord of this House, for the covenant of the journey of winter and summer).

Quraysh are the descendants of al-Nadr ibn Kinanah; whoever is born of al-Nadr is Qurashi, and whoever is not born of al-Nadr is not Qurashi.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We are the sons of al-Nadr ibn Kinanah; we do not trace our mother's lineage, nor do we deny our father" [263] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/211.]].

Abu Bakr al-Jawzi informed us, saying: al-Ru'uli related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abu al-Mughirah related to us, saying: al-Awza'i related to us, saying: Abu Ammar Shaddad related to us, from Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Allah, mighty and majestic, chose Banu Kinanah from the sons of Isma'il, and chose from Banu Kinanah Quraysh, and chose from Quraysh Banu Hashim, and chose me from Banu Hashim" [264] [[Kitab al-Sunnah: 618; and Musnad Abi Ya'la: 13/472.]].

They were named Quraysh from al-taqarrush, which means earning, moving about, gathering and seeking, for they were a people keen on wealth and generosity.

Mu'awiyah asked Abdullah ibn Abbas: Why was Quraysh named Quraysh? He said: After a creature in the sea called al-qirsh, which eats and is not eaten, and rises above and is not risen above. He said: Do the Arabs know that in their poetry? He said: Yes:

"Quraysh is the one who dwells in the sea, by which Quraysh was named Quraysh.
It has sent its armies to rise in the depths of the sea over all the seas.
It eats the rotten and the fat, and leaves in it no feather for one with two wings.
Thus in the lands is the tribe of Quraysh, devouring the lands with a sharp devouring.
And for them at the end of time is a prophet who causes much killing and wounding among them,
who fills the earth with his horses and men, who make the mounts gasp with a swift, hard gasp."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/203; Fath al-Bari: 6/388. Al-Khamus: scratches on the body; al-Kamish: swift.]]

His saying "ilaafihim" is a substitution (badal) for the first "al-ilaaf" and a shortened form of it. Whoever drops the yā' from "al-ilaaf" relies on the verse of Abu Talib, advising Abu Lahab concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

"Do not abandon him, as long as you live, to one who would belittle him, and be a man of valour and chastity,
who repels the enemies from a Hashimite company; otherwise they would be the best of people in covenant."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/202.]]

"Rihlata al-shita' wa al-sayf": scholars differed on the grammatical basis for the accusative of "rihlah." It was said: it is put in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning their departure was a journey. If you wish, you may make it accusative by the occurrence of "ilaafihim" upon it; if you wish, as an adverb of place, meaning "during a journey"; if you wish, you may make them both in the nominative, meaning "they are the journeys of winter and summer." The first is more wondrous and more beloved to me, because it is written in the mushafs without a yā'.

As for the exegesis: Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn Abbas, who said: They used to spend winter in Makkah and summer in al-Ta'if, so Allah commanded them to spend winter in the Haram and to worship the Lord of the House.

Abu Salih said: In Syria there was a cold land and a hot land. They would travel in winter to the hot land and in summer to the cold land. They had two journeys each year for trade: one in winter to Yemen, because it is warmer, and the other in summer to Syria. The Haram was a barren valley without crops or herds, without water or trees, and Quraysh only lived there through their trade and journeys, and no one would attack them.

They used to say: Quraysh are the residents of Allah's Haram and the custodians of His House. Had it not been for the two journeys, no one would have stayed in Makkah, and had it not been for the security of being neighbours of the House, they would not have been able to conduct their affairs. Thus travel to Yemen and Syria was hard for them. Tabalah, Jarash and al-Jund in the lands of Yemen were fertile, so they carried food to Makkah: the people of the coast by ship over the sea, and the people of the land by camels and donkeys. The people of the coast unloaded at Jeddah, and the people of the land at al-Muhassab. Syria was also fertile, so they carried food to Makkah: the people of Syria carried it to al-Abtah, and the people of Yemen carried it to Jeddah. They obtained provisions nearby, and Allah relieved them of the burden of the two journeys and commanded them to worship the Lord of the House.

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Abu al-Walid Hassan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Zakariyya al-Mutarriz related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: Abu Awanah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), with Abu Bakr, passed by a group of them reciting:

"O you who seek generosity and liberality, why did you not pass by the family of Abd al-Dar?"

"If you passed by them seeking their hospitality, they would have forbidden you from hardship and poverty."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr: "Is this how the poet said it, O Abu Bakr?" He said: No, by the One who sent you with truth, rather he said:

"O you who seek generosity and liberality, why did you not pass by the family of Abd Manaf?"

"If you had passed by them seeking their hospitality, they would have forbidden you from hardship and distress."

"The ones who strip away, and there is none who strips away, and those who say 'come, for the guests!'"

"And those who mix their wealthy with their poor, until their poor become like the sufficient."

"And those who say with every true promise, while the men of Makkah are in years of drought, lean."

"Two journeys, which he established for himself and his people: the journey of winter and the journey of summer."

Al-Kalbi said: The first to carry the wheat (al-samra') from Syria and to send camels on its journeys was Hashim ibn Abd Manaf.

*liyaʿbudū* (let them worship): the lām of command. *Rabba hadha al-bayt alladhi at'amahum min ju'in* (the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger).

Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Abu al-Fadl Ubaydullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Ja'far related to us, saying: I heard Ibn Malik ibn Dinar say: No nation has fallen from the eye of Allah, glorified be He, except that its livers were struck with hunger.

*Wa-amanahum min khawf*: that is because they used to say, "We are the custodians of Allah's Haram, so no one shall confront them in the Jahiliyyah." Even if a man was struck in one of the tribes of the Arabs, he would say, "My sanctuary, my sanctuary," and he would be left alone with his property, out of reverence for the Haram. Whereas whoever else of the Arab tribes went out, he would be raided.

Al-Dahhak, al-Rabi', Shurayk and Sufyan said: "Wa-amanahum min khawf" means: from leprosy, so that leprosy would not afflict them in their land.

We were also informed by Abu al-Hasan al-Muqri, saying: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Isa al-Muqri al-Burujirdi related to us in Baghdad, saying: Abu Sa'id Umar ibn Mirdas related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bukayr al-Hadrami related to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Abdullah related to us, from [Abu] Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Salim, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The dust of Madinah cures leprosy" [266] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 12/236, from Ibn al-Sunni and Abu Nu'aym in al-Tibb.]].

Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, said: "Wa-amanahum min [khawf]" means that the caliphate would be only among them [267] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/209; the bracketed text is from it.]].

Yahya ibn Ubaydullah al-Sulami related to us, saying: Nuh ibn Abi Maryam related to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah of Li-ilaafi Quraysh will be given the reward of ten good deeds, equal to the number of those who circumambulated the Ka'bah and performed i'tikaf in it" [260] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/449.]].

And al-Husayn informed me, saying: Hazim ibn Yahya al-Halwani related to us, saying: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Thabit, who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Atiq informed me, from Sa'id ibn Umar ibn Ju'dah, from his father, from his grandmother Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah favoured Quraysh with seven qualities that He gave to no one before them and will give to no one after them: Allah favoured Quraysh in that I am of them, prophethood is among them, the hijabah (custodianship of the Ka'bah) is among them, the siqayah (provision of water to pilgrims) is among them, He gave them victory over the elephant, they worshipped Allah, glorified be He, for twenty years with none worshipping Him besides them, and Allah revealed a surah concerning them in which no one other than them is mentioned" [261] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 12/27.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

For the covenant (li-ilaafi) of Quraysh, their covenant.

The reciters differed regarding it. Abdullah ibn Amir read (li-alaaf), with hamza, shortened vowel, and without a yā' (ي). Abu Ja'far read (ilaaf) without hamza, seeking only lightness (li-ilaafi), with the yā' hamzated and elongated. As for their reading (ilaaf): al-Umari related from Abu Ja'far, and al-Balkhi from Ibn Kathir, (ilfihim) with the lām sukun and without a yā'. Confirming this reading is what

al-Husayn ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Khunays related to us, saying: Abu Khadijah Ahmad ibn Dawud related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan ibn Layth, from Shamir ibn Hawshab, from Asma', who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) [recite]: "Ilfihim rihlat al-shita' wa al-sayf" [262] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/394.]].

Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan related with his chain from Abu Ja'far, and al-Walid from the people of Syria (ilafihim), with hamza, shortened vowel, and without a yā'. Muhammad ibn Habib al-Hamawi related from Abu Yusuf al-A'sha, from Abu Bakr, from Asim (i'alfihim), with two hamzas, the first kasrah and the second sukun. The rest read (iilaafihim).

Sa'id ibn al-Ma'afa informed us, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, who said: Abu Karnab related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Abu Makki, from Ikrimah, that he used to read (iliyalaf Quraysh alfihim).

Some of them counted the two surahs as one; among them Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and there is no separation between them in his mushaf.

Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: We had an imam who did not separate them, and he would recite them together. Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi said: I prayed the Maghrib behind Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and he recited in the first rak'ah "Wa al-tini wa al-zaytun," and in the second "Alam tara" and "Li-ilaafi Quraysh."

They differed regarding the cause that brings in this lām. Al-Farra' said: it is connected to the preceding surah, for He, exalted is He, reminded the people of Makkah of His great blessing upon them in what He did to the Abyssinians; then He said: "li-ilaafi Quraysh," meaning: We did that to the companions of the elephant as a blessing from Us upon Quraysh, that is, Our blessing upon them in their journeys of winter and summer. It is as if He said: a blessing upon a blessing, so the lām carries the meaning of (ila, "to").

Al-Razi and al-Akhfash said: it is the lām of wonder. The meaning is: "Wonder at the covenant of Quraysh, the journey of winter and summer, and their abandonment of worship of the Lord of this House," and then He commanded them to worship Him.

This is like one saying in speech: "For Zayd, and our honouring him," in the manner of wonder, meaning: I marvel at that. When the Arabs bring this lām, they suffice with it as evidence of wonder, making the verb apparent in it, like the words of the poet:

"Does it deceive you that they said Qurrah is a poet? O father of him, of a ʿarīf and a poet!"

That is, wonder at Qurrah being a poet.

It was also said that it is the lām of purpose (kay), its meaning being "fa-ja'alahum ka-'asfin ma'kul" (He made them like eaten chaff) "to bring Quraysh together," so the destruction of the companions of the elephant was the cause of the continuance of Quraysh's covenant and the order of their condition and the wealth of their people. Al-Zajjaj said: it refers to what follows it, its estimate being: "liya'budu rabba hadha al-bayt li-ilaafi rihlat al-shita' wa al-sayf" (so that they may worship the Lord of this House, for the covenant of the journey of winter and summer).

Quraysh are the descendants of al-Nadr ibn Kinanah; whoever is born of al-Nadr is Qurashi, and whoever is not born of al-Nadr is not Qurashi.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We are the sons of al-Nadr ibn Kinanah; we do not trace our mother's lineage, nor do we deny our father" [263] [[Musnad Ahmad: 5/211.]].

Abu Bakr al-Jawzi informed us, saying: al-Ru'uli related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abu al-Mughirah related to us, saying: al-Awza'i related to us, saying: Abu Ammar Shaddad related to us, from Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Allah, mighty and majestic, chose Banu Kinanah from the sons of Isma'il, and chose from Banu Kinanah Quraysh, and chose from Quraysh Banu Hashim, and chose me from Banu Hashim" [264] [[Kitab al-Sunnah: 618; and Musnad Abi Ya'la: 13/472.]].

Mu'awiyah asked Abdullah ibn Abbas: Why was Quraysh named Quraysh? He said: After a creature in the sea called al-qirsh, which eats and is not eaten, and rises above and is not risen above. He said: Do the Arabs know that in their poetry? He said: Yes:

"Quraysh is the one who dwells in the sea, by which Quraysh was named Quraysh.
It has sent its armies to rise in the depths of the sea over all the seas.
It eats the rotten and the fat, and leaves in it no feather for one with two wings.
Thus in the lands is the tribe of Quraysh, devouring the lands with a sharp devouring.
And for them at the end of time is a prophet who causes much killing and wounding among them,
who fills the earth with his horses and men, who make the mounts gasp with a swift, hard gasp."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/203; Fath al-Bari: 6/388. Al-Khamus: scratches on the body; al-Kamish: swift.]]

His saying "ilaafihim" is a substitution (badal) for the first "al-ilaaf" and a shortened form of it. Whoever drops the yā' from "al-ilaaf" relies on the verse of Abu Talib, advising Abu Lahab concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

"Do not abandon him, as long as you live, to one who would belittle him, and be a man of valour and chastity,
who repels the enemies from a Hashimite company; otherwise they would be the best of people in covenant."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/202.]]

"Rihlata al-shita' wa al-sayf": scholars differed on the grammatical basis for the accusative of "rihlah." It was said: it is put in the accusative as a verbal noun, meaning their departure was a journey. If you wish, you may make it accusative by the occurrence of "ilaafihim" upon it; if you wish, as an adverb of place, meaning "during a journey"; if you wish, you may make them both in the nominative, meaning "they are the journeys of winter and summer." The first is more wondrous and more beloved to me, because it is written in the mushafs without a yā'.

As for the exegesis: Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn Abbas, who said: They used to spend winter in Makkah and summer in al-Ta'if, so Allah commanded them to spend winter in the Haram and to worship the Lord of the House.

Abu Salih said: In Syria there was a cold land and a hot land. They would travel in winter to the hot land and in summer to the cold land. They had two journeys each year for trade: one in winter to Yemen, because it is warmer, and the other in summer to Syria. The Haram was a barren valley without crops or herds, without water or trees, and Quraysh only lived there through their trade and journeys, and no one would attack them.

They used to say: Quraysh are the residents of Allah's Haram and the custodians of His House. Had it not been for the two journeys, no one would have stayed in Makkah, and had it not been for the security of being neighbours of the House, they would not have been able to conduct their affairs. Thus travel to Yemen and Syria was hard for them. Tabalah, Jarash and al-Jund in the lands of Yemen were fertile, so they carried food to Makkah: the people of the coast by ship over the sea, and the people of the land by camels and donkeys. The people of the coast unloaded at Jeddah, and the people of the land at al-Muhassab. Syria was also fertile, so they carried food to Makkah: the people of Syria carried it to al-Abtah, and the people of Yemen carried it to Jeddah. They obtained provisions nearby, and Allah relieved them of the burden of the two journeys and commanded them to worship the Lord of the House.

Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Abu al-Walid Hassan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Zakariyya al-Mutarriz related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: Abu Awanah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), with Abu Bakr, passed by a group of them reciting:

"O you who seek generosity and liberality, why did you not pass by the family of Abd al-Dar?"

"If you passed by them seeking their hospitality, they would have forbidden you from hardship and poverty."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr: "Is this how the poet said it, O Abu Bakr?" He said: No, by the One who sent you with truth, rather he said:

"O you who seek generosity and liberality, why did you not pass by the family of Abd Manaf?"

"If you had passed by them seeking their hospitality, they would have forbidden you from hardship and distress."

"The ones who strip away, and there is none who strips away, and those who say 'come, for the guests!'"

"And those who mix their wealthy with their poor, until their poor become like the sufficient."

"And those who say with every true promise, while the men of Makkah are in years of drought, lean."

"Two journeys, which he established for himself and his people: the journey of winter and the journey of summer."

Al-Kalbi said: The first to carry the wheat (al-samra') from Syria and to send camels on its journeys was Hashim ibn Abd Manaf.

*liyaʿbudū* (let them worship): the lām of command. *Rabba hadha al-bayt alladhi at'amahum min ju'in* (the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger).

Abu Abdullah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Abu al-Fadl Ubaydullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Ja'far related to us, saying: I heard Ibn Malik ibn Dinar say: No nation has fallen from the eye of Allah, glorified be He, except that its livers were struck with hunger.

*Wa-amanahum min khawf*: that is because they used to say, "We are the custodians of Allah's Haram, so no one shall confront them in the Jahiliyyah." Even if a man was struck in one of the tribes of the Arabs, he would say, "My sanctuary, my sanctuary," and he would be left alone with his property, out of reverence for the Haram. Whereas whoever else of the Arab tribes went out, he would be raided.

Al-Dahhak, al-Rabi', Shurayk and Sufyan said: "Wa-amanahum min khawf" means: from leprosy, so that leprosy would not afflict them in their land.

We were also informed by Abu al-Hasan al-Muqri, saying: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Isa al-Muqri al-Burujirdi related to us in Baghdad, saying: Abu Sa'id Umar ibn Mirdas related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bukayr al-Hadrami related to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Abdullah related to us, from [Abu] Bakr ibn Muhammad, from Salim, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The dust of Madinah cures leprosy" [266] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 12/236, from Ibn al-Sunni and Abu Nu'aym in al-Tibb.]].

Ali, may Allah ennoble his face, said: "Wa-amanahum min [khawf]" means that the caliphate would be only among them [267] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/209; the bracketed text is from it.]].
